bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta report comments[0].content / staged vulnerable source / static PoC parse / saved sanitizer trace
bug_description.normalized: The staged 2172-byte sfnt blob reaches HarfBuzz's subsetter and the `name` table path. Static inspection of the vulnerable file and source shows the `name` directory entry claims file offset 1896 and length 600, but `hb_blob_create_sub_blob()` can only materialize the 276 bytes remaining in the file. Vulnerable `OT::name::sanitize()` then accepts that truncated table after only shallow header checks: `format=0`, `count=20`, `stringOffset=4`, the 20-record array fits inside 276 bytes, and `stringOffset` itself is in range. Because `sanitize()` never calls `sanitize_records()` / `NameRecord::sanitize()` on each record, the individual `NameRecord.offset` and `length` fields remain unchecked. During subsetting, the default `name_ids` set is expanded to `0..0x7FFF`, so `name::subset()` keeps ordinary-name records from that shallow-sanitized array. Static parsing of the staged blob shows the first selected non-empty out-of-range record is index 8 with `nameID=3221`, `length=251`, and `offset=2156`; with `stringOffset=4`, that string span ends at table-relative byte 2411, far beyond the 276-byte blob. `NameRecord::copy()` therefore passes an out-of-range source pointer into `serialize_copy()`, `UnsizedArrayOf::copy()` copies 251 bytes from outside the `name` blob into serializer object storage, and `pop_pack()` then inserts that packed object into `packed_map`. HarfBuzz hashes and compares packed objects by dereferencing their byte contents, so the copied non-font bytes reach the deduplication hashmap and MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` in `hb_hashmap_t::item_t::is_unused()`.

root_cause.description: The vulnerable sanitizer accepts the `name` table after only shallow header and array-range checks; it never dispatches `NameRecord::sanitize()` on each record against the string pool.
root_cause.note: The staged fix adds `&& sanitize_records (c)` here. For the staged blob, the shallow checks succeed on `format=0`, `count=20`, `stringOffset=4`, even though record 8 later contributes `offset=2156` and `length=251`, a span that lies far beyond the actual 276-byte table blob.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness is accepted far enough as an OpenType font container for `hb_face_create()` to retain a face object and later expose the `name` table directory entry.

name_table_selected.description: When source-table enumeration reaches the `name` tag, the subsetter dispatches that table into `_subset2<const OT::name>`, putting the malformed `name` records on the observed crash path.

evidence_limitations: The staged artifacts prove the dangerous record span is out of range, but they do not identify the exact runtime address outside the `name` blob that `src_base + 2156` aliases on the reproduced run.

MSAN's origin names unrelated heap pages used by `plan->name_ids`; that origin explains where the copied poisoned bytes came from at runtime, not the actual project-side defect, which is the missing per-record validation in `OT::name::sanitize()`.

fine_trace.note: On the truncated blob from step 1, the header still reads `format=0`, `count=20`, and `stringOffset=4`. The 20-record array fits inside 276 bytes and `stringOffset` itself is in range, so this shallow sanitizer returns success without ever checking whether any individual `NameRecord.offset/length` span stays inside the string pool.

Subsetting iterates the shallow-sanitized `NameRecord` array through the default `name_ids` filter, which `hb_subset_plan_create()` expanded to `0..0x7FFF` when the input set was empty. Static parsing of the staged blob shows the first selected non-empty out-of-range record is index 8 with `nameID=3221`, `length=251`, and `offset=2156`; with `stringOffset=4`, its referenced span ends at table-relative byte 2411, far beyond the 276-byte blob.

fine_trace.note: When step 3 reaches record 8, `NameRecord::copy()` turns the unchecked fields into the concrete source span `src_base + 2156` for 251 bytes. That span starts well past the 276-byte `name` blob and even past the 2172-byte witness buffer.

fine_trace.code: out->arrayZ[i] = arrayZ[i]; /* TODO: add version that calls c->copy() */
fine_trace.note: The serializer copies `count=251` bytes from the out-of-range source pointer from step 4 into a new `UnsizedArrayOf<HBUINT8>` object. These bytes are no longer validated font data; on the reproduced run MSAN traces them back to unrelated heap state from the `name_ids` allocation chain.

After the out-of-range copy from step 5, `pop_pack()` moves the 251-byte serialized object from the serializer head region into packed storage at the tail. This preserves the copied poisoned bytes as the canonical packed-object contents.

The packed object from step 6 becomes a key in `packed_map`, HarfBuzz's deduplication hashmap. For this key type, `hb_hash(key)` and equality both dereference `*obj` and operate on the object's byte contents, so the bytes copied in step 5 become hash/comparison input.

fine_trace.code: bool is_unused () const    { return key == kINVALID; }
fine_trace.note: MSAN sink. `packed_map.set()` from step 7 enters bucket lookup in `hb_hashmap_t`, and the saved trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` here while deduplicating the serialized object built from steps 5-6.

allocation_context.note: The saved MSAN origin says the poisoned bytes were created by a heap deallocation via `realloc` here, reached through `hb_set_t::add_range()` while `hb_subset_plan_create()` populated the default `name_ids` set.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: MSAN's origin identifies whichever unrelated heap bytes the unchecked `NameRecord` copy happened to read at runtime, while the logical project bug is `OT::name::sanitize()` accepting the table without running `NameRecord::sanitize()` on each record.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged fix adds `sanitize_records (c)` to `OT::name::sanitize()`, which dispatches `NameRecord::sanitize(c, string_pool)` for each record before the table is accepted. That rejects the staged record-8 span (`stringOffset=4`, `offset=2156`, `length=251`, end=2411`) because it lies outside the actual 276-byte `name` subblob.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the crash by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_14641 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which reported `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in the packed-map path while `hb-subset-fuzzer` processed `poc`.

format.name: Malformed sfnt/TrueType font blob
format.contract: The staged PoC is the exact 2172-byte sfnt blob in `gt_results/arvo_14641/poc`. Static parsing of that file and the vulnerable source shows the `name` directory entry claims file offset 1896 and length 600, so HarfBuzz materializes only the remaining 276 bytes as the `name` table blob. The vulnerable `name` sanitizer still accepts that blob because its header reads `format=0`, `count=20`, and `stringOffset=4`, and the 20-record array itself fits inside 276 bytes. Within those 20 records, the first selected non-empty out-of-range record under the default `name_ids` filter is index 8 with `nameID=3221`, `length=251`, and `offset=2156`, so its referenced string span ends at table-relative byte 2411, far beyond the 276-byte blob. `NameRecord::copy()` therefore serializes bytes from outside the `name` table into the packed-object dedup path, which is the exact trigger relationship justified by the staged artifacts; they do not support a broader input contract beyond this witnessed malformed font structure.
